channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Moraes indica defensor público para defesa de Tagliaferro e marca nova audięncia
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes has ordered the Federal Public Defender's Office to represent Eduardo Tagliaferro, his former aide at the TSE, and scheduled a new hearing in the case.

item.title: PF prende dono da Choquei, MC Ryan e Poze do Rodo em operaçăo contra lavagem de dinheiro
item.description: Federal Police arrested the owner of Choquei, MC Ryan, and MC Poze do Rodo in a money laundering operation. The arrests occurred the same day as a Genial/Quaest poll showed Lula leading alone in the first round of the 2026 elections, with Flávio having a numerical advantage in the second round, according to analysis by Josias de Souza and Leonardo Sakamoto. Additional highlights include app drivers protesting against PLP 152 in São Paulo and NASA releasing new details about the Artemis II astronaut rescue.

item.title: Lula lidera no 1ş turno e Flávio tem vantagem numérica no 2ş, diz Quaest; Josias e Sakamoto analisam
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll released on April 15, 2026 shows President Lula (PT) leading in isolated first-round voting intentions for the 2026 elections. In a potential runoff, Flávio Dino holds a numerical advantage over his likely opponent. Columnists Josias de Souza and Leonardo Sakamoto analyze the results, highlighting the current political landscape.

item.title: Senador petista é hospitalizado e passará por cirurgia no quadril
item.description: Senator Paulo Paim (PT-RS) was hospitalized at Sírio-Libanês Hospital after tests indicated the need for hip surgery. He had previously disclosed health issues last year when deciding not to run for Senate re-election. Paim reaffirmed his commitment to support, as much as possible, the PT’s electoral project in Rio Grande do Sul and President Lula’s re-election campaign.

item.title: Decisão de Moraes contra Flávio pode fortalecer uma narrativa na guerra eleitoral
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes' decision to authorize an investigation against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for alleged defamation of President Lula has reignited the debate over the boundaries between free speech and criminal liability, after Bolsonaro accused Lula of drug trafficking and money laundering without evidence. While political criticism is part of democratic discourse, analysts argue that unsubstantiated serious accusations may cross the line into slander, and the probe could shape electoral narratives—bolstering a persecution narrative among his base while potentially harming his appeal among broader voters.

item.title: Moraes nega visita de irmão de Michelle para cuidar de Bolsonaro
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes denied the defense's request to allow permanent visitation by Michelle Bolsonaro's brother to Jair Bolsonaro's residence under humanitarian house arrest. The ruling states that only healthcare, security professionals, and previously authorized individuals may enter, rejecting family or domestic reasons as valid grounds. Moraes emphasized there is no technical justification for the exception, as the individual is not a healthcare professional.

item.title: Pesquisa Quaest: velocidade de Flávio e votos soltos embaralham disputa com Lula
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll reveals a polarized race between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, with the senator gaining rapid momentum as the consolidated figure of Bolsonarism. Although Lula still leads, his advantage has narrowed, and the second round shows a technical tie. The significant share of undecided or blank/null voters remains a key factor that could determine the outcome.

item.title: Flávio diz que inquérito de Moraes sobre Lula tenta “cercear liberdade”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) criticized Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes' decision to authorize an investigation against him for alleged slander against President Lula, calling it legally weak and an attempt to restrict freedom of speech. He argued his January 2026 post, which linked Lula to Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and mentioned potential whistleblowing, merely reported publicly known facts about Maduro's imprisonment without directly accusing Lula of crimes. Flávio compared the move to what he described as electoral imbalance by the TSE in 2022 and affirmed his constitutional duty to oversee the government.

item.title: Nomes de indicados ao CNMP são aprovados na CCJ e vão a Plenário
item.description: The Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) unanimously approved the nominations of Márcio Barra Lima and Carl Olav Smith for the National Council of the Public Ministry (CNMP). The candidates were questioned on public safety and investigative powers, receiving 22 votes in favor. The nominations will be voted on in the Plenary later this Wednesday.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio Bolsonaro avaliam que entrada de Caiado na eleição leva disputa ao 2º turno
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) believe that Ronaldo Caiado's (PSD) entry into the 2026 presidential race will guarantee a runoff, which they view as positive for the opposition campaign. They see Caiado's candidacy as fragmenting the government-aligned bloc and increasing the opposition's chances of victory.

item.title: Deputado aciona TJ para que Alerj não realize eleição interna até decisão do STF
item.description: State Deputy Luiz Paulo (PSD) filed a writ of security with the TJ of Rio to prevent Alerj from convening internal elections for the presidency of the House until the STF decides on the format of the supplementary election for the state government. The action aims to avoid internal proceedings before the judicial definition of the state election. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: Lula sai em defesa de Papa em mensagem à Igreja Católica após ataques de Trump
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva issued a message defending Pope Leo XV after criticism from Donald Trump, who claimed credit for the pope’s election and accused him of being too political. Lula stated that defenders of peace have been attacked by powerful figures who see themselves as deities, emphasizing that love for one’s neighbor outweighs the power of weapons and money. He also referenced the National Conference of Bishops of Brazil (CNBB) and its role in defending democracy and opposing the military dictatorship.

item.title: STF AO VIVO – Nepotismo em cargos políticos e quebra ampla de sigilo – sessão de 15/4/2026
item.description: The STF resumes the hearing of two extraordinary appeals: RE 1.133.118, examining whether the anti-nepotism rule applies to political offices such as municipal or state secretary and federal minister; and RE 1177984, concerning whether the state must inform suspects of their right to silence during police approach or only during formal interrogation. Also on the agenda are RE 1301250, challenging judicial authorization for breaking internet search history secrecy without defined suspects (linked to the Marielle Franco case), and the joint judgment of ADPF 342 and ACO 2463, assessing the constitutionality of Law 5.709/71 restricting rural land purchases by Brazilian companies with foreign capital.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes avalia acionar PGR contra Alessandro Vieira
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes is considering filing a criminal complaint against Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) for alleged abuse of authority, after Vieira requested the indictment of STF ministers and the Attorney General in the Organized Crime CPI, a request rejected by the committee. Mendes argues the report overstepped the CPI’s authority by attempting to initiate impeachment proceedings against justices, characterizing it as an electoral move and an attack on democratic institutions.

item.title: Em mensagem a católicos, Lula manifesta solidariedade ao papa Leão XIV em episódio envolvendo Trump
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva expressed solidarity with Pope Leo XIV, stating that defenders of peace are often attacked by powerful figures who see themselves as divine. The remarks came amid criticism from U.S. President Donald Trump, who called the pope 'weak' and 'terrible in foreign policy' for advocating diplomatic solutions to international conflicts.

item.title: Reforma Casa Brasil: governo amplia crédito para reforma de moradias para quem tem renda até R$ 13 mil
item.description: The federal government expanded the Reforma Casa Brasil program, raising the maximum family income eligible for credit from R$9,600 to R$13,000, increasing the maximum loan amount from R$30,000 to R$50,000, cutting interest rates to 0.99% per month for all income brackets, and extending the repayment term from 60 to 72 months. The FGHab will now guarantee all loans, with Caixa Econômica Federal as the operator. Announced in an election year, the initiative targets Brazil’s structural housing deficit by financing renovations of existing homes, not just new construction.

item.title: Janja vai à Espanha antes de Lula para agenda sobre feminicídio
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula da Silva advanced her trip to Spain to attend an agenda focused on combating femicide, including a visit to the VioGén system, meetings with equality authorities, and a stop at the Centro Cometa in Madrid. The itinerary reinforces her role as a public policy articulator on women's rights, a government priority in an election year, given that 53% of Brazil's electorate is female.

item.title: Agência de comunicação vence licitação em SP e atenderá governos Lula e Tarcísio
item.description: Communication agency Calia Y2 controlled by FSB won bidding to serve São Paulo government and Presidency with a R$ 300 million per year contract.

item.title: Comissão debate indícios de aumento abusivo nas contas de água e esgoto da Sabesp
item.description: The Consumer Defense Committee of the Chamber of Deputies is debating, this Thursday (16), indications of abusive increases in water and sewage bills from Sabesp following meter replacements, with reports of bill hikes up to 100% without corresponding consumption changes. Deputy Kiko Celeguim (PT-SP) states that the official 6.11% adjustment for 2026 does not explain these increases, highlighting economic and social impacts, especially on low-income families, alongside frequent supply failures that make the billing contradictory. The hearing will address Arsesp’s role, review measures, refunds, and consumer compensation.

item.title: Motta banca vitória de petista para o TCU e sela aliança com partido
item.description: Allies of House Speaker Hugo Motta (Republicans-PB) advised postponing the TCU ministerial vote due to the risk of defeat for his supported candidate, Odair Cunha (PT-MG). The pressure came just hours before the session, reflecting concern over the outcome.

item.title: O que tem piorado avaliação de Lula, segundo economistas
item.description: Lula's approval is declining due to growing public perception of economic deterioration, with 71% feeling a loss of purchasing power and 72% noticing higher supermarket prices. Economists describe this as a 'recession vibe' driven by inflationary corrosion, particularly affecting food and transport, which erodes real income for low-income families despite modest official growth.

item.title: A seis meses da eleição, governo anuncia ampliação do programa de reforma de casas para quem ganha até R$ 13 mil
item.description: The federal government announced an expansion of the home renovation program, raising the income eligibility cap from R$ 9,600 to R$ 13,000, standardizing the interest rate at 0.99%, and increasing the credit limit from R$ 30,000 to R$ 50,000 with a repayment term extended to 72 months. President Lula stated the move aims to reduce housing costs and pressure the Central Bank to lower the Selic rate, while the Minister of Cities confirmed a R$ 20 billion allocation from the Social Fund for housing, bringing the total budget to R$ 200 billion.

item.title: ‘A direita diz que Ramagem foi preso por multazinha, mas ele foi condenado por golpe’, diz Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that former deputy Alexandre Ramagem, arrested by ICE in the U.S., was convicted in Brazil for attempting a coup and must return to serve a 16-year sentence. Lula dismissed right-wing claims that the arrest was over a minor fine, emphasizing Ramagem is a fugitive after conviction for armed criminal organization, coup d'état, and violent abolition of the democratic state. The arrest followed international cooperation between the Brazilian Federal Police and U.S. authorities, after Ramagem fled Brazil using false documents.

item.title: Lula sugere a empresários da construção civil que enviem cartas para senadores a favor de Messias
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva urged construction industry leaders to send letters to senators supporting the nomination of Jorge Messias to the Supreme Federal Court (STF), citing his strong defense of the FGTS fund. The appeal followed a speech by André Baía, director of the North and Northeast Construction Industry Forum, who praised Messias as a guardian of workers’ severance funds and shared a personal connection from their childhood church. The nomination hearing was moved up to the 28th, and Messias requires at least 41 Senate votes for approval in the plenary.

item.title: Análise: Lula não reverte piora na avaliação, e preço dos alimentos e dívidas são os principais desafios
item.description: The Quaest poll shows President Lula with 40% approval and 52% disapproval, while Flávio Bolsonaro leads with 42% in voting intentions for 2026. The government's declining approval is driven by rising food prices (up from 59% to 72% reporting increases in the last month) and growing household indebtedness (up from 65% to 72% reporting little or lots of debt). Perception that the economy worsened over the past year reached 50%, compared to only 21% seeing improvement.

item.title: A leitura do mercado financeiro após nova pesquisa entre Lula x Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Financial markets show an incipient expectation of power alternation in the 2026 elections, driven by polls suggesting Lula trails Flávio Bolsonaro, but emphasize this reading is preliminary and subject to change as the electoral landscape evolves, including alliances, use of public resources, and campaign dynamics. Investors avoid definitive bets, awaiting clarity in the political chessboard before confidently pricing assets.

item.title: Entre o Ceará e a presidência, Ciro Gomes vira problema para o PL
item.description: The PSDB signaled support for Ciro Gomes' presidential candidacy in 2026, causing tension within the PL, which had previously backed him only for the Ceará gubernatorial race. PL leadership, including Michelle Bolsonaro, views the move as a predictable betrayal, fearing Ciro could siphon votes from both Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, threatening a right-wing runoff. The PSDB aims to reposition Ciro as a national alternative to polarization.

item.title: Governo Lula quer aplicação imediata do fim da escala 6 X 1
item.description: The Lula government advocates for the immediate implementation of ending the 6x1 work schedule, without an adaptation period, through a bill allowing alternatives like 5x2 or 4x3 via collective bargaining. The argument is that cost impacts would be offset by productivity gains, citing a business that reduced absenteeism after voluntarily switching. Congressional sectors call for a gradual transition, while Ipea studies indicate the impact resembles a real minimum wage increase, except in labor-intensive sectors like security and cleaning, where a phased approach is suggested.

item.title: Em tom de brincadeira, Lula diz que vai conversar com Galípolo e afirma que juros podem cair se BC 'olhar para pessoas como ele'
item.description: President Lula jokingly said he will talk to Central Bank President Gabriel Galípolo to push for lower interest rates, arguing that if the BC 'looks at people like him' — a metalworker and working-class figure — rates would fall. He emphasized that the government is also attending to the middle class, citing families earning between R$ 9,000 and R$ 11,000 who want to stop renting and buy their own homes, and noted that programs like Minha Casa, Minha Vida and Reforma Casa Brasil were expanded to serve this group.

item.title: Lula pede que brasileiro “denuncie” posto que cobra mais por combustível
item.description: The Lula government launched a public campaign urging Brazilians to report fuel stations charging abusive prices, despite tax cuts and financing measures aimed at mitigating the impact of the Middle East war on fuel and cooking gas prices. The one-minute video, aired on TV, X (@CanalGov), and YouTube, emphasizes the federal tax exemption on diesel and biodiesel, financing of imported cooking gas and airfare subsidies, and a hotline for reporting price gouging (08009700267). The Secom did not disclose campaign costs or media spending.

item.title: Lula quer fim imediato de jornada 6x1 e mandou projeto porque Câmara postergava, diz ministro
item.description: Labor Minister Luiz Marinho said the Lula government wants immediate approval of ending the 6x1 work schedule by Congress, claiming that related bills in the Chamber were being delayed. The proposal aims to abolish the six-day workweek with one day off, taking effect immediately after legislative approval.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes rebate fala de Zema sobre impeachment e cita dívida de MG com União: ‘Irônico'
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes rebuked former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema's statements defending the impeachment and arrest of STF ministers, calling the remarks ironic and referencing Minas Gerais' debt to the federal government.

item.title: A vantagem de Flávio Bolsonaro sobre Lula em grupo estratégico
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro extended his lead over Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva among independent voters, increasing his advantage from 5 to 7 percentage points in a potential runoff. The senator reached 33% voting intention, compared to 26% for the president, while 36% of independents reject both candidates. The shift, which began last month, has solidified Bolsonaro as the frontrunner in this pivotal voter bloc for the 2026 election.

item.title: Novo Plano Nacional de Educação é sancionado e entra em vigor
item.description: President Lula sanctioned the new National Education Plan (PNE) for 2026-2036, setting goals such as universal preschool access, literacy for 80% of children by the end of 2nd grade, and increasing public education investment to 10% of GDP by 2036. The plan includes 19 objectives, 73 goals, and 372 strategies across all education levels, with biennial monitoring by Inep and mandatory alignment of state and municipal decennial plans.

item.title: A reação de Flávio à abertura de investigação no STF por suposta calúnia contra Lula
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, labeled the STF's opening of an investigation against him for alleged slander against President Lula as censorship, claiming he only reported facts about Nicolás Maduro and that the inquiry seeks to restrict his freedom of expression. He denied committing any crime, accused Minister Alexandre de Moraes of using the judiciary to silence opposition, and demanded the Lula government explain its ties to the Venezuelan dictatorship. The investigation was authorized by Moraes following a PGR opinion, based on a January X post linking Lula to drug trafficking and money laundering, alleging he would be implicated by Maduro.

item.title: MST ocupa fazenda no Nordeste e pressiona governo Lula por mais assentamentos
item.description: Around 500 MST members occupied Fazenda Córrego in Ceará, claiming the property has over 300 hectares of unproductive land. The action is part of the National Struggle Day for Agrarian Reform, commemorating the 30th anniversary of the Eldorado do Carajás massacre and demanding stronger settlement policies from the Lula government.

item.title: Fim da jornada 6x1: os argumentos de quem é contra e quem é a favor
item.description: The Lula government has sent a bill to Congress to end the 6x1 work schedule, reducing the weekly workload from 44 to 40 hours, guaranteeing two paid rest days and prohibiting any salary reduction. Classified as a constitutional urgency, the proposal aims to improve workers’ quality of life, align Brazil with global trends, and boost productivity based on international experiences. Supporters emphasize health and well-being benefits, while critics warn of uncalculated economic impacts on society.

item.title: CCJ da Câmara analisa projeto que acaba com a escala 6x1; ASSISTA
item.description: The Chamber's Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) is reviewing proposals to end the 6x1 work schedule, reducing the weekly workload to 36 hours and guaranteeing three days off. The proposals include a PEC by Deputy Erika Hilton (PSOL-SP) and Deputy Reginaldo Lopes (PT-MG), along with the Lula government's plan, which allows maintaining the 12x36 schedule in collective agreements if the weekly average remains at 40 hours.

item.title: Só 17% no Brasil dizem que transporte público é plenamente acessível, diz Ipsos
item.description: In Brazil, only 17% of respondents strongly agree that public transport is fully accessible, while 33% somewhat agree, indicating low perceived service quality. Despite this, there is strong support for sustainable mobility policies, including bike lane expansion (65%), preference for walking or cycling (59%), and congestion pricing (51%). Interest in electric vehicles remains low at 36%, below the global average of 47%.

item.title: Datafolha diz que 29% acreditam que o Brasil ganhará a Copa
item.description: Datafolha reported that 29% of Brazilians believe Brazil will win the 2026 World Cup, the lowest level in the historical series, down from 33% in July 2025. France ranked second at 17%, followed by Argentina and Germany at 4% each. 35% of respondents did not express an opinion. The survey was conducted in person from April 7–9, 2026, with 2,004 respondents aged 16 or older across 137 municipalities, and a margin of error of 2 percentage points.

item.title: Como Gilmar, Fachin e Toffoli reagiram ao relatório de Vieira na CPI do Crime Organizado
item.description: STF ministers rejected the Organized Crime CPI report calling for the indictment of Alexandre de Moraes, Dias Toffoli, Gilmar Mendes, and Paulo Gonet, labeling it legally baseless, an abuse of authority, and politically motivated. Flávio Dino defended the Court’s role in fighting organized crime and called the criticisms a 'historic mistake'. Edson Fachin firmly opposed the inclusion of ministers in the report, while Dias Toffoli called it an 'excrescence' and suggested the rapporteur, Alessandro Vieira, could be declared ineligible.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula anuncia medidas para o setor habitacional
item.description: President Lula announces measures to sustain growth in the housing sector, joined by ministers and government officials. The actions aim to boost the economy through housing investments and credit. The announcement takes place this Wednesday at 10:30 AM, with live broadcast.

item.title: Indústria vai em peso para Alemanha para feira de tecnologia que homenageará o Brasil
item.description: Over 260 Brazilian industrialists are attending Hannover Messe in Germany, where Brazil is the honored country. The mission, led by the CNI, includes bilateral agendas, visits to companies like Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen, and the annual Brazil-Germany Economic Meeting, with the opening ceremony attended by President Lula and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

item.title: Tesouro lança 3 títulos em euro com vencimento até 2036
item.description: The Brazilian Treasury issued three euro-denominated bonds in international markets, maturing in 2030, 2033, and 2036, marking the first such issuance in over a decade. Led by BBVA, BNP Paribas, Bank of America, and UBS, the move aims to diversify Brazil's public debt currency exposure beyond the U.S. dollar.

item.title: Messias busca oposição após PL e Novo se posicionarem contra indicação ao STF
item.description: Union Attorney General Jorge Messias is intensifying efforts to secure support for his Supreme Court nomination after the PL and Novo parties announced they would vote against him, citing institutional instability. Despite formal opposition, he is pursuing personal outreach via holiday messages and leveraging the quiet support of Justice André Mendonça, who is working behind the scenes to ease conservative resistance, while banking on secret voting to overturn public declarations of opposition.

item.title: Projeto vincula cota mínima de candidatas à proporção de mulheres na população
item.description: Bill 1155/26 proposes linking the minimum quota of female candidacies in elections to the proportion of women in the Brazilian population, based on IBGE Census data, replacing the current fixed 30% floor with a dynamic criterion. Based on the 2022 Census showing women at 51.5% of the population, the minimum quota would rise to that figure, rounded up. The 70% maximum for any gender would be retained, and the TSE must publish the applicable percentage at least 12 months before each election.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Governo envia novo texto da escala 6×1 mesmo com PECs avançando na Câmara
item.description: The Lula government sent a new bill to Congress to reduce the workweek, even as two related PECs are already advancing in the Chamber. Relator Paulo Azi deemed the PECs admissible and criticized the government's move as unnecessary and potentially disruptive. Despite possible delays from opposition requests for vista, approval of the proposals is still expected.

item.title: O que está por trás da dúvida de Lula sobre a própria candidatura
item.description: President Lula sparked speculation about his 2026 re-election bid after stating he has not yet decided whether to run, citing low popularity, Flávio Bolsonaro’s rise in polls, and external factors like the Iran war and the Banco Master scandal. While some advisors question the risk of a potential defeat, the government maintains Lula as the presumptive candidate without seriously discussing a 'Plan B'. His remark may reflect dissatisfaction with his approval ratings, an effort to energize the PT, or a tactic to unsettle opponents — but his true intentions remain known only to him.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vira alvo de inquérito por calúnia contra Lula
item.description: The Federal Police opened an inquiry against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) for possible slander against President Lula, after he posted on social media an image associating the president with Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro and accusing him of crimes such as drug trafficking, arms trafficking, money laundering and electoral fraud without evidence. The investigation was authorized by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, with an initial 60-day deadline, and proceeds in the STF due to the senator's privileged forum.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: percepção de moderação de Flávio Bolsonaro cresce, enquanto medo da família recua e empata com Lula
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows a slight increase in the perception of Flávio Bolsonaro as moderate (from 38% to 39%), while negative views of him decreased (from 48% to 45%). Fear of the Bolsonaro family returning to power fell to 43%, now tying with fear of Lula’s government (40-42%), signaling a more balanced risk perception. In a hypothetical runoff, Bolsonaro leads Lula 42% to 40% — a technical tie, but the first time he trails numerically ahead.
